messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The audio encoder is part of the proposed conditional recurrent adversarial video generation network structure." -- cites: E1 (Section 1): quote "The inputs to the network are collected by the following feature extraction modules. Audio Feature Extraction Given an entire audio sequence A , we use a sliding window to clip the audio file into several audio segments."; E4 (Figure 2): observation "The figure shows the audio encoder as part of the network structure."

Cited evidence:
[E1] (text, Section 1, page 3): order to solve these problems, we propose a hybrid recurrent feature generation modeling scheme to capture both the visual and audio dependency over time. We use a recurrent neural network to ingest both the image and audio sequential signal and generate the image sequence directly from a decoder network. We will explain the detailed design in the following section. 3.2 Conditional Recurrent Video Generation In order to map independent features to a sequence of correlated ones, we apply the recurrent unit on the hybrid features to enforce the temporal coherence on both image and audio signals. Our proposed conditional recurrent video generation network is illustrated in Fig. 2. The inputs to the network are collected by the following feature extraction modules. Audio Feature Extraction Given an entire audio sequence A , we use a sliding window to clip the audio ﬁle into several audio segments. In Fig. 2, each A t represents the Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefﬁcients (MFCC) features of each audio segment. We further feed each audio MFCC feature A t into an audio encoder E A to extract the audio feature z A

verdicts.reason: The evidence from E1 (Section 1) states that the audio feature extraction is part of the network inputs, and E4 (Figure 2) shows the audio encoder as part of the network structure. This supports the claim that the audio encoder is part of the proposed conditional recurrent adversarial video generation network structure.
